extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of political science, history, and social institutions; educated general readers interested in American political/economic development
extracted.subtask_description: A chapter-length analytical forecast about the future of American political, social, and economic institutions, identifying indicators of progress, sources of danger, and structural advantages affecting democratic stability over coming decades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of national leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: The Presidents of this generation are abler and more high-minded men than those of 1834–1860, and neither the members of a knot of party managers nor its creatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as an indicator of political progress: capable, independent executives (versus party-controlled figures) signal healthier institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diminished poisonous influence of slavery
rubrics_metrics.description: The poisonous influence of slavery is no longer felt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The removal of slavery's corrosive political effects is treated as a precondition for moral and political improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced sentimentalism with maintained earnestness
rubrics_metrics.description: There is every day less of sentimentalism, but not less of earnestness in political discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for sober, earnest debate over mere sentimental rhetoric as a mark of maturation in public discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decline of blind party obedience
rubrics_metrics.description: There is less blind obedience to party, less disposition to palliate sins committed from party motives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A healthy polity shows increasing independence of voters and officials from rigid party loyalties; party-based excusing of misconduct is a negative sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher standard of purity among public men
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard of purity among public men, especially in the Federal government, is higher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public probity at high levels (federal) is a concrete metric of institutional improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth and quality of public intellectual engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of able men who occupy themselves with scientific economics and politics is larger; their books and articles are more widely read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Growth of informed public debate and professional expertise indicates strengthening civic institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the press and pulpit in reform
rubrics_metrics.description: The press more frequently helps in the work of reform: the pulpit deals more largely with questions of practical philanthropy and public morals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active, reform-minded media and religious discourse supporting public morals are positive contributors to civic improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Youth engagement as a positive sign
rubrics_metrics.description: That it should be taken as a good sign when the young men of a city throw themselves into politics, shows that the new generation is believed to have either a higher sense of public duty or a less slavish attachment to party ties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Youth participation in politics signals either elevated civic duty or reduced partisan submission; treat as an optimistic indicator.

rubrics_metrics.name: National humility and receptivity to criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: They have become more modest, and listen willingly to speakers and writers who descant upon their failings. They feel themselves strong enough to acknowledge their weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A society's willingness to heed criticism and admit faults is taken as a healthy moral development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical-comparative judgement
rubrics_metrics.description: To judge of America rightly the observer must not fix his eye simply upon her present condition... He must look back at what the best citizens and the most judicious strangers perceived and recorded seventy, forty, twenty years ago.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess contemporary conditions relative to past reports; evidence that formerly darker 'shadows' have lessened supports claims of progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust in time/reason and moral tone of the majority
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Americans say... that they trust to time, they mean that they trust to reason, to the generally sound moral tone of the multitude, to a shrewdness which after failures and through experiments learns what is the true interest of the majority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidence in gradual improvement through public reason and moral advancement is presented as a strategy for democratic progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural advantages aiding democratic stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Three great advantages — an absence of class distinctions and class hatred, a diffusion of wealth among an immense number of small proprietors, an exemption from chronic pauperism and economical distress — provide stability and a safety valve in the West.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These structural features are evaluated as buffers that allow peaceful adjustment and social mobility, reducing revolutionary risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immigration as a mixed influence; source of danger when unassimilated
rubrics_metrics.description: European immigration continues, and though more than two-thirds of the immigrants make valuable citizens, the remainder, many by their political ignorance and instability... are a source of danger to the community, lowering its tone, providing material for demagogues to work on, threatening outbreaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immigration is assessed quantitatively and qualitatively; lack of assimilation or political instability among newcomers is a danger to civic order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental/economic limits and resulting pressures
rubrics_metrics.description: As she fills up her western regions... all the best land... will have been occupied... the land now under cultivation will have been so far exhausted as to yield scantier crops... the struggle for existence will become more severe... cities will have grown immensely more populous; pauperism... may be more widely spread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resource exhaustion, loss of frontier outlet, and urban crowding are foreseen structural pressures that can test democratic institutions; plan policies accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of anarchy despite crises
rubrics_metrics.description: One thing... need not be apprehended... there will not be anarchy. The forces which restore order and maintain it when restored are as strong in America as anywhere else in the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even under stress, built-in social/order-restoring mechanisms are expected to prevent total breakdown; recognize but not exaggerate risk of anarchy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporations and trusts as political problems requiring regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies... are so useful that any general diminution of the legal facilities for forming them seems improbable; but I conceive that they will be even more generally than hitherto subjected to special taxation; and that their power of taking and using public franchises will be still further restricted... The next few years or even decades may be largely occupied with the effort to deal with these phenomena... Their solution will demand... great legal skill, but great economic wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Growth and concentration of corporate power (including trusts) is identified as a problem: policies may include special taxation, limiting franchises, and legal/economic reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence of small proprietors in agriculture as stabilizing factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Almost the only great landed estates are in the Far West... Taking the country as a whole, there is no indication of any serious change to large properties... The system of small proprietors tilling the soil they live on... contributes to the happiness and stability of the commonwealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintenance of small landholdings is seen as socially stabilizing and unlikely to be easily displaced; agricultural aggregation is less worrisome than industrial aggregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Urban migration and changing population composition
rubrics_metrics.description: For many years past there has been an indraught of people from the rural districts to the cities... the transfer of people from a rural to an urban life goes on... because of economic causes and a distaste for farm isolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Urbanization trends alter social composition and may degrade rural 'flower' of population; monitor urban social conditions and attendant political effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assimilative power of American institutions over immigrants
rubrics_metrics.description: The amazing solvent power which American institutions, habits, and ideas exercise upon newcomers of all races... The children of Irishmen, Germans, and Scandinavians are certainly far more like native Americans than the current views of heredity would have led us to expect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural and institutional assimilation is a mitigating factor against perceived long-term harm from heterogeneous immigration; use assimilation indicators when assessing impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic growth of great fortunes and political effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The most remarkable economic feature... has been the growth of great fortunes... The growth of vast fortunes has helped to create a political problem, for they become a mark for the invective of the more extreme sections of the Labour or Socialist parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentration of wealth is both persistent and politically salient; anticipate legislative or regulatory responses directed first at corporations rather than individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional economic shifts and development opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Immigration is already turning from the North-west towards the Southern region... Western North Carolina, Northern Georgia and Alabama, and Eastern Tennessee possess enormous mineral deposits... as the vacant spaces of the West are ceasing to be able to receive settlers, these Southern regions will more and more attract settlers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shifts in settlement and regional resource exploitation will reshape social and political alignments; monitor migration flows and development potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Race relations and need for patience and sympathy
rubrics_metrics.description: The negro is doubtless a heavy burden for American civilization to carry... Much patience will be needed, and much sympathy... Their progress since emancipation has been more rapid than those who saw them in slavery expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Race-related social problems require long-term policy attention, education, and empathetic measures; do not ignore moral/political costs in forecasts.
